name: Stoneness
description: Occulting bright light, eclipsed every 2 secs.

name: Broadness
description: Occulting light, bright 3 secs., eclipsed 7 secs.

name: Northfleet
character: One occulting bright or red light, ½ min.
description: Red iron frame on India Arms wharf. Light eclipsed 3 secs. in every ½ minute. Bright in fairway of Northfleet Hope and Gravesend Reach; red over anchorage in Gravesend Reach and over Broadness

name: Ovens Flat
description: Gas-lighted buoy, showing an occulting light

name: Mucking Flat
character: One occulting bright or red light, ½ min.
description: Red pile lt.-ho. Lt. red N. of E. by S. ½ S. over Scar Elbow, and a narrow red ray to S. ½ E. over W. Blyth buoy. Red W. of S.W. ¾ W. over Ovens Spit. Bright elsewhere. Eclipsed 3 secs. in every ½ min.

name: Chapman Head
character: One occulting bright or red light, ½ min.
description: Red pile lt.-house. Light is bright in fairway channel; red over Leigh Middle to North of S.E. by E. ¾ E. Light eclipsed for 3 secs. twice in quick succession in every ½ minute

name: Southend Pier-head
description: One fixed red light

name: Sheerness
description: Gas light on N.W. face of circular fort on Garrison Point. Not visible North of N.N.W. Gas-lighted buoys, each showing an occulting light, are placed at East Oaze Sand, and Sheerness Middle Ground

name: Queenborough
description: 1. Two red leading lts. on pier, in line S. 7° W. 2. A bright light is shown from beacon on extr. of Queenborough Spit, in 6 ft. water

name: NORE LIGHTVESSEL
character: One rev. br. lt., ½ min.
description: In 4 fathoms, at East end of the Nore Sand. Painted red, with ball at mast-head

name: Girdler Lightvessel
character: One rev. br. lt., ½ min.
description: In 3½ fathoms, West Girdler Sand, at West entrance of Princes Channel. Red, with ball

name: Princes Channel Lt.-Ves.
description: In 4 fms., North side of channel, betw. Girdler and Tongue lightvessels. Red, with ball

name: Tongue Lightvessel
description: In 10 fms., North side of East Tongue Sand. Red, with ball. Lt. gives one red flash and one bright flash in quick succession every ½ min.

name: Margate Pier
description: Column, 70 ft. high, at West end of pier. Also a small green light on end of jetty

name: Mouse Lightvessel
description: In 4 fathoms, at West end of Sand. Red, with ball

name: Maplin Pile Lighthouse
character: One occulting red light, ½ minute
description: Painted red. Lt. eclipsed 3 secs. in ev. ½ min., not vis. over the sand; a bright ray to S. ¾ W. betw. Girdler light and Shivering Sand buoy. Bright lt. shown 13 ft. below main lt. to S.E. by E. ¾ E. over Spit buoy Maplin Spit Buoy carries an occulting bright gas light

name: Swin Middle Lightvessel
character: One rev. br. lt., ½ min.
description: In 5½ fathoms, at West end of Sand. Red, with ball

name: Gunfleet Pile Lighthouse
character: One rev. red lt., ½ min.
description: On S.E. side of Sand; keep ½ mile off, and do not pass to North. Painted red

name: SUNK LIGHTVESSEL
description: In 7 fms., nearly 2 miles S.E. ½ E. from West Rocks buoy; red & br. flash alternately; half ball above ball. Telegraph cable to Walton

name: LONG SAND HEAD LT.-VESSEL
description: In 11 fathoms, 2 miles E. ¾ N. from Long Sand Head buoy. Red, with diamond at mast-head. Two quick flashes, followed by 20 secs. eclipse

name: KENTISH KNOCK LT.-V.
description: In 11 fathoms, on East side of Sand. Red, with two red balls vertically

name: GALLOPER LT.-VESSEL
description: In 20 fathoms, on S.W. side of Shoal; lights horizontal. Red, with ball on each mast

name: NORTH FORELAND
character: One occulting bright or red light, ½ min.
description: White tower, 85 ft. high. A strip of red light to East end of Margate Sand, betw. N. by E. and N. by W. ¾ W. Light eclipsed for 5 secs. in every ½ minute

name: Ramsgate
character: 1. One fixed red or green light on West pier 2. Green lt. on W. cliff 3. Green lt. on E. cliff 4. Occulting br. lt., 10 secs., on East pier
description: 1. Red lt. while 10 ft. and upwards in entrance, or from 2¾h. before, to 3½h. after high water; green light when less than 10 ft. 2. Green light in one with West pier lt. leads through Old Cudd Channel 3. Green light in one with West pier light leads through Ramsgate Channel 4. Visible 5 secs., eclipsed 5 secs. Also two red lts., vertical, on promenade pier

name: GOODWIN LT.-VESSEL
description: Off North end of the Goodwin Sands, in 10 fathoms. Light shows 3 flashes in quick succession, followed by 36 secs. eclipse. Red, three masts and balls

name: EAST GOODWIN LT.-V.
description: About 1½ mile to the eastward of the Goodwin Sands, in 30 fathoms. Red, with half diamond over diamond at mast-head

name: Gull Stream Lightvessel
description: On the West side of the Goodwin Sands, in 8 fathoms. Red, with ball

name: S. SAND HEAD LT.-VES.
description: Off the South end of the Goodwin Sands, in 14 fathoms. Red, with ball at mast-head. Light shows flash of 1½ sec., eclipsed 6 secs., flash of 5 secs., and then eclipsed 17½ secs.

name: Deal Iron Pier
description: A fixed red light on pier-head

name: SOUTH FORELAND
description: White buildings. In line W. ¾ N., 385 yards apart, clear South end of Goodwin. High light visible betw. N.E. by N. & W. by S. ½ S.; low light betw. N.E. ¾ E. and W. by S. ½ S.

name: DOVER
description: Red tower, 30 ft. high, on end of Admiralty Pier. A flash every 7½ secs.

name: Dover Harbour
character: One fixed green light Fixed red Tide lights
description: One red lt. on North pier while 7 ft.; one red lt. on South pier while 7 to 10 ft.; two red lts. while above 10 ft. The green lt. at West side of entrance to Granville Dock

name: Folkestone
character: 1. Fix. red & bright lts. 2. One fixed green or br. light
description: 1. On S. pier-head a red light while 12 ft.; a bright lt. below it when above 14 ft.; when red light is blinked occasionally, use caution 2. On new railway pier, a green light seaward, but bright inshore of danger

name: VARNE LIGHTVESSEL
description: In 15 fathoms, at West end of the shoal. Red, with ball at mast-head

name: DUNGENESS
character: 1. One fix. br. or red lt. 2. One flashing bright light every 5 secs.
description: 1. Tower, 92 ft. high, with red & white belts, about 450 yds. from H.W. mark. Red lt. over W. anchorage northward of W., and red lt. over E. anchorage West of N.E. by E. ½ E. 2. Tower on extremity of point, 675 ft. S.E. by S. ½ S. from main light

name: Rye
character: 1. Two fixed bright lts. 2. One fixed red light
description: 1. On East pier, 850 yards apart N. by W. Upper light when 10 ft. on the bar. Lower light shown until half-ebb 2. On groyne, West side of entrance. Shown until half-ebb

name: Hastings
description: Bright lt. on West Hill, red lt. on beach; in one, N.N.E., 300 yards apart, to direct the fishermen. A green light on the pier

name: R. SOVEREIGN SHOALS
description: Lt.-vessel in 12 fms., South, E.-ly, 2 miles from Royal Sovereign buoy. Shows 3 flashes in 23 secs., at intervals of 37 secs. Small ball over usual mast-head ball (In summer of 1887, light will be altered to triple-flashing ev. 45 secs.)

name: Eastbourne
description: A fixed green light on the new pier

name: BEACHY HEAD
description: White tower, 47 ft. high, on summit of Belle-tout Cliff. From the eastward the light will open when bearing N.W. by W., and by keeping it so will lead 1½ mile outside Royal Sovereign Shoals (In summer of 1887, light will be altered to show a flash of 4 secs. in every 15 secs.)

name: Newhaven
character: 1. One fixed bright lt. 2. One fixed Tide light
description: 1. Wood framework, on outer extr. of E. pier 2. Lt.-ho., 55 ft. high, on outer extr. of West pier. Under 10 ft. on bar, lt. is green; 10 to 14 ft., red; over 14 ft., bright. Two small red lts. near end of break-water in progress. A small green lt. on each pier, 200 yds. within entr

name: Brighton Chain Pier
description: One fixed green light

name: ,, Pile Pier
description: One fixed red light

name: Shoreham Harbour
character: One fixed bright light, and Tide light Two fixed green lights
description: Tide lt. on central pier, green while 8 to 11 ft., bright while 11 ft. and over, and red at high water; bears S. by W. ½ W., 250 yards from upper fix. br. lt. Two green lts., one on E., one on W. pier-head. Approaching, keep high bright lt. open E. of W. pier green lt.

name: Worthing Pier
description: A fixed bright light on the pier

name: Littlehampton
character: Fix. red lt. and Tide lts.
description: White lt.-ho., 40 ft. high, on N. end of E. pier. Tide lts. on S. end of pier: bright 10 ft., green 11 ft., red 12 ft., red and bright 13 ft., two bright 14 ft., bright and green 15 ft., till high water. In line, North, lead to entrance

name: Selsea Bill
character: One fix. green or red lt.
description: Light green between East and S. ½ E., thence red to S.W. by W. Fishing light

name: OWERS LIGHTVESSEL
description: Off S. end of Shoal, in 16 fms. A flash every ½ min., alternately br. & red. Red, with ball

name: Nab Lightvessel
description: In 5½ fathoms, near New Grounds; must be passed to eastward. Red, with balls

name: ST. CATHERINE'S PT.
description: Stone tower, 84 feet high. Light visible between E. ¾ S. and N.W. ½ W.

name: Warner Lightvessel
description: In 13 fathoms, on the eastern part of the shoal. Red, with ball

name: Ryde Pier
description: Also green light on West side, and red and green lights on East side of pier-head

name: SPITHEAD
description: Green light on fort at Brading Haven; bright light on No Man's Land Fort, with red sector of 14° over Ryde Sand Head and Sturbridge Shoal; red light on Horse Sand Fort; bright light on Spit Sand Fort

name: Stokes Bay Pier
description: Red lights on East and West ends. Two others shown when steamers expected

name: Southsea Castle
character: One fix. red or green lt.
description: Shows red in channel betw. Spit Refuge Buoy and Horse Fort, or between S. ¾ W. and S.W. by S. ½ S.; thence green to West of the Spit Buoy to W. ½ S.

name: Southsea
description: Two red lights on Clarence Esplanade Pier. Also bright light when steamers plying

name: Portsmouth Harbour
character: One fixed red or green light
description: On South end of South railway jetty. Shows red on East side of harbour to S.E. tangent of Block House Fort, and green westward of that line. Small lts. shown at landing-piers

name: Calshot Lightvessel
description: Off Calshot Castle, on East side of channel, in 3½ fathoms. Red, with ball

name: Calshot Spit Lightvessel
character: Two fixed lts., bright and red
description: In 6 fathoms, near S.E. extremity of Spit. Two masts, with conical cages. One light on each mast; high light red. Bell buoy replaced when vessel needs repairs

name: Netley Pier
description: One fixed green light

name: Hythe Pier
description: Two fixed red lights, vertical

name: Southampton
character: 1. Two fixed red lts. 2. Two fixed green lts. 3. Two fixed lights 4. Two fixed lights
description: 1. On either side of entrance to Docks. In one, N.E. by N. ½ N., lead up River Itchen in 14 ft. 2. On Extension Quay, N.W. side of R. Itchen 3. Red over bright, from lt.-vessel, at entrance of River Itchen 4. Red lt. on Royal Pier, green lt. on Town Pier

name: Yarmouth
description: In winter. Green outer light near castle wall; inner bright lt. In one, S.S.W., lead into the harbour. A fix. red lt. on end of wooden pier

name: NEEDLES OUTER ROCK
character: One occulting bright, red, or green light, ½ minute
description: Granite tower, 109 feet high, white with one black band. Light eclipsed 3 secs. every ½ min., shows red to South from S.E. ¾ S. to W. ¾ S.; thence bright over entrance of Needles Channel to W. by N. ¾ N.; thence red up the Channel to N.E. ½ E.; thence bright to N.E. by E., to clear Warden Ledge; and green thence to the land

name: Totland Bay
description: A fixed green light on the pier

name: Hurst Beach
description: White towers, 85 and 52 ft. high, 223 yards apart N.E. by E. ¼ E., in rear of fortifications. High light visible between S.W. ¾ W. and W. by S. ¾ S., low light between S.W. and W. by S. ½ S. Leading light shown from high lt.-ho. up the Solent, betw. E. & E. by N. ½ N.

name: Bournemouth
description: A fixed red light on the pier

name: Poole
description: In one, N. ¾ W., 786 ft. apart, on North side of entrance; low lt. masked betw. S. ½ W. and S. by W. ¼ W. Red lights at town in winter

name: DURLSTON HEAD
description: White lighthouse, 39 ft. high, on Anvil Point, West part of head. A flash every 10 secs., visible between about W. ½ N. and E. by N.

name: Weymouth
description: Red lights near beach, East of railway station, in line bear N. by W. ¾ W. Green lights on North pier in line bear West

name: PORTLAND
description: White towers, 50 & 85 ft. high, 1,509 ft. apart, near the Bill. In one, N.W. by N., lead between Race and Shambles. Low light only shown between N.W. by W. ¾ W. and E.N.E.

name: Portland Breakwater
description: On centre of fort, at extremity. Lt. obscured by peninsula betw. S.S.W. and W. by S. ½ S.; & betw. W. by S. ½ S. & W.N.W. lt. is obscured to an observer 15 ft. above the sea when within 2 miles of Chesil Bank

name: SHAMBLES SHL. LT.-V.
description: At East end of shoal, in 15 fathoms. Flash of 5 secs., eclipse 6 secs., flash 1½ sec., eclipse 17½ secs. Red, with ball

name: Lyme Regis
description: In one, N.W. ½ N., 825 feet apart. Leading lights to inner pier-heads

name: Sidmouth
description: A fixed bright light on West side of creek

name: Exmouth
description: Two fixed red or bright lights

name: Teignmouth
description: One on a limestone tower, on S.W. end of Denn; the other on a house; lead to fairway

name: Babbacombe
description: Fishing light, green to N.E., red seaward, bright to S.W.

name: Torquay
description: Bright light on inner pier, showing red to westward; red light on outer pier

name: Brixham
description: Green light on West pier-head, and red light on end of breakwater

name: Dartmouth
character: 1. One fixed bright, red, or green light 2. One fixed bright lt. 3. One small fix. bright, red, or green light
description: 1. On Kingswear or North side; bright light towards fairway, betw. S. ½ E. and S. by E. ¾ E.; thence red light to the land, and green light to S.W., between S. ½ E. and the land, or over Checkstone, Pin Rock, &c. 2. S. by E., 110 feet from former; in one lead up fairway 3. Near Coast-guard Station; bright in fairway, red over shoals on N. side of harbour, and green light over shoal of One Gun Point to S.

name: START POINT
character: One rev. br. lt., 1 min., and fixed bright light
description: White tower, 92 feet high. A fixed light at 181 ft. is shown over Skerries Rocks between N.E. ¾ E. and E. ½ S. Signal Station to S.

name: Plymouth Breakwater
character: One occulting bright or red light, ½ min. Lower fixed bright light
description: Granite tower, 76 ft. high, on W. end. Light eclipsed 3 secs. every ½ min.; bright seaward, betw. E. by S. ½ S. and N.E. ½ E., through South, and red over the anchorage. A lower bright light is seen when channel is open, between S.W. ¾ W. and S.W. by W. ¾ W.

name: Plymouth Harbour
description: Bright light on West Barbican pier-head; red lts. on Millbay piers, and also one at Mount Wise landing. Occulting bright light, 5 secs., on extremity of Mount Batten Breakwater

name: EDDYSTONE
character: One 2-flashing br. lt., ½ min., & low fix. br. lt.
description: New granite lt.-ho., 168 ft. high, S. by E. ¾ E. from old tower. Two quick flashes in every ½ min. A lower fix. br. lt. shown over Hand Deeps, betw. N.W. by N. ½ N. and N.W. ¾ W.

name: Fowey
description: A fixed red harbour light

name: FALMOUTH
character: 1. One rev. br. lt., 20 s., and lower fixed br. lt. 2. Two fixed green lts.
description: 1. White lt.-ho., 62 ft. high, on St. Anthony Point. The lower lt. shows betw. S.W. by S. ½ S. and S. by W., to clear Manacle Rocks 2. On ends of breakwaters

name: LIZARD
description: Two white towers, each 61 ft. high, W. by N. and E. by S., 223 ft. ayart, on the Lizard Cliff. In one lead clear of the Manacles, and Wolf Rk. A signal & telegraph station on Beast Pt., about ¾ of a mile to E.

name: WOLF ROCK
description: A noble granite tower, 143 feet high. Flashes red and bright alternately

name: Penzance
description: On the South pier-head. Red, or when less than 15 ft. water green, betw. E. by S. ¾ S. and S. by W. ½ W.; the remainder bright. By day, a ball while 15 feet

name: LONGSHIPS
character: One occulting bright or red light, 1 min.
description: Gray granite tower, 117 ft. high. Lt. suddenly eclipsed for 3 secs. every minute. Bright light seaward, from N.E. by N. ½ N., or half a mile West of Brisons Rocks, to S. by E. ½ E., or ¾ of a mile West of Runnelstone; red in-shore of these bearings

name: SEVEN STONES LT.-VES.
description: On East side of rocks, in 40 fathoms; red, with ball. Shows three quick flashes, followed by 36 secs. darkness

name: SCILLY
character: One rev. br. lt., ½ min.
description: White tower, 74 feet high, on summit of St. Agnes Island. Obscured by islands from N. ½ E. to E. ½ S.

name: BISHOP ROCK
description: A noble granite tower, 147 feet high, on the S.W. rock. Lt. invisible to eastward betw. N.E. ¾ E. and E. ½ S., except to E. by N. Light shows two quick flashes of 4 secs. each, followed by 48 secs. eclipse. Lighthouse being heightened, and light will gradually be elevated to 143 ft.

name: St. Ives
description: On inner pier-head, while 10 ft. water; from September 1 to April 30. Also a fixed red light near end of outer wooden pier

name: Hayle
character: 1. Two fix. br. Tide lts. 2. One fixed red light
description: 1. On W. side of entrance; in one S. by W. ¾ W., 297 feet apart; shown while 12 feet water... 2. On jetty of Lelant Quays

name: GODREVY
character: One flash. br. lt., 10 secs. Lower fixed red light
description: Stone tower, 86 ft. high, on the island. Lower red light shown over Stones Rocks, between N.W. and N. by W.

name: Padstow
description: A fixed red or green light on quay head

name: TREVOSE HEAD
description: White tower, 87 ft. high, on N.W. extremity. Light eclipsed 3 times in quick succession in 15 secs., and then visible for 45 secs.

name: HARTLAND POINT
description: White tower, showing one flash at intervals of 30 secs., two bright and one red

name: LUNDY ISLAND
character: One rev. br. lt., 2 min. Lower fixed bright light
description: In one white tower, 96 feet high, half a mile from South end of island. Low light visible to West between N. by W. and S.W.

name: BIDEFORD
description: White towers, 311 yards apart, on Braunton Sands, N. side of entrance. In one, S.E. ½ E., lead over bar. High light vis. betw. W.S.W. and N.N.W.; obscured betw. N.N.W. and E. ½ N., over Baggy Leap and Asp Rks.; a lt. of less power vis. in harb. from E. ½ N., through South, to W.S.W. Low lt. only shown from half-flood to half-ebb, while 15 ft. over bar; appears full between West and N.W. by N. ½ N.

name: BULL POINT
character: One 3-flash. br. lt., ½ m., and lower fixed red lt.
description: White tower. Light shows three quick flashes, followed by 18 secs. darkness, every ½ min. Red light, 18 ft. lower, shows betw. W. by S. and N.W. by W. ½ W., to mark Morte Stone

name: Ilfracombe
description: Fix. red lt. on Lantern Hill. (Sept. 1 to Apl. 30)

name: Minehead
description: Fix. gr. lt. on pier, 3h. before to 2½h. after H.W.

name: Watchet Breakwater
description: Fixed red Tide light, 8 ft. flood to 10 ft. ebb...

name: Burnham, or Bridgewater
character: Upper light occulting bright, 1 min. Lower light fixed bright or red
description: On East side of entrance to River. In one, E. by S. ½ S., 1,500 ft. apart. High lt. eclipsed twice in quick succession, then visible for 54 secs.; white tower, 99 ft. high. Low light, square tower, 36 ft. high, with black streak; bright between W. ¾ N. and W.N.W.; red over the bar between W. by N. and W. ½ N.; and red up the river between S. by W. and S. by W. ½ W.

name: Clevedon
description: One fixed red light on pier-head

name: Portishead
description: One fixed bright light on pier

name: Breaksea Lightvessel
description: In 18 fathoms, 2 miles N.W. by W. ¾ W. from One-fathom Bank buoy. Red, with ball ...

name: Avon
character: One occulting br., red, or green lt., ½ min.
description: White tower, 65 ft., on E. side of channel. Lt. eclipsed 3 secs. in ev. ½ min. A red sector to N.W., & a green ray from W. to W. by S. at turn of channel. A fix. red lt. 230 yds. to N.W.

name: Avonmouth
description: Low lt. from red hut on N.W. pt. of Dumball Id., high lt. from pole on white hut on mainland, 750 yds. to E. by S.; leading lights through King Road. Lights at Avonmouth Dock entrance, red on North side, blue on South side

name: English & Welsh Grounds
description: Lightvessel on South side of channel, in 4½ fathoms. Red, with ball.

name: New Passage
description: Lights on piers and Charstone Rk. for steamers

name: River Severn
description: 1. One fix. Tide lt. on N. pier-hd. of tidal basin. 1 red lt. N.E. of pier when specially required 2. Red light on centre pier, and bright light at landward extreme of each wide arch .........

name: FLATHOLM
character: One occult. br. or red lt.
description: White tower, 99 ft. high, on South point. Lt. eclipsed 3 secs. twice in ev. ½ min.; red betw. N.W. ¾ W. and N. by W. ½ W.; thence bright to N. ½ W., from Ranie Spit Shoal to West Cardiff buoy; and thence red to N.E.

name: Usk (Newport)
character: One fixed bright, red, or green light
description: White tower, 57 ft. high, on West side. Light bright betw. S.W. by W. ¾ W. and S.S.W.; thence red to S. by E. ½ E.; thence bright over river entrance to S.E. by S. ½ S.; thence red to the land. Green up the river between E. by N. ½ N. and N.E. by E. ½ E.........

name: Cardiff
description: Two red lights, about 23 yards apart, and two bright lights, near docks. A bright light on Bute Dock pier-head .........................

name: NASH POINT
character: Two fixed bright lights, and lower fixed red lt.
description: White towers, 111 & 60 ft. high, 1,000 ft. apart, N.W. by W. ¾ W. In line lead South of Nash Sand. High lt. red North of S.E. ½ E., and from a window below a red light is shown over Tuskar Rock, between N.W. ½ N. and N.W. by N. Low light obscured North of N.N.W., and high light North of N.W. ½ W. ........................

name: Porthcawl Harbour
character: 1. One fixed bright, red, or green light 2. Two fixed red lights
description: 1. On S.E. end of breakwater. Bright betw. S.W. by W. ½ W. and W. by N. ½ N.; red to North and green to East of this sector......... 2. Horizontal, on inner part of breakwater, when gates are open ................................

name: Briton Ferry
description: Three Tide lights on East training wall .........

name: Neath
description: Two fixed br. Tide lts. on end of training wall

name: Swansea Harbour
character: 1. One fixed red Tide lt. 2. One fixed bright lt. 3. One fixed bright lt. 4. Two green or red lts. 5. Two green or red lts. 6. One green or red light
description: 1. White tower on West pier-head; shown while 8 ft. water, April 1 to Nov. 30, and while 10 ft. during winter. Black ball by day 2. On inner part of W. pier, vis. only to eastwd. 3. Electric light on East pier-head .............. 4. and 5. At South dock, vertically; at North dock, horizontally; red when closed, green when open ............................ 6. At New Cut bridge; red when closed ......

name: Scarweather Sand Lt.-V.
description: Off West end of Sand, in 14 fathoms. Red, with half globe above usual globe..............

name: MUMBLES
description: White tower, 56 feet high, on outer islet ......

name: Helwick Lightvessel
description: In 16½ fathoms, off West end of Sand. Red, with ball at mast-head............................

name: Llanelly
description: One on Whiteford Point (on piles) from half-flood to half-ebb; other from half-flood to quarter-ebb on South end of breakwater ...

name: Burry Port
description: Near head of West pier while 10 feet water

name: Saundersfoot, South Pier
description: One fixed red light or yellow ball while 8 feet

name: Tenby Pier Head
description: One fixed red Tide light for steamers, &c.

name: CALDY ISLAND
character: One occulting bright or red light, ½ min.
description: White tower, 52 ft. high, on S. part of island. Light eclipsed for 3 secs., once in every ½ minute; bright seaward; red towards Old Castle Head, from W. by N. ¾ N. to N.W. by W., and over Woolhouse Shoal from N. by E. ½ E. to N.E. ¾ E.

name: MILFORD HAVEN ST. ANN'S POINT
description: White towers, 75 and 42 ft. high, 610 ft. apart, on W. side. In line, N.N.W., lead in clear of Crow and Toes Rocks. A red ray from high lighthouse shows over Chapel and Harbour Rocks between S.E. and East.

name: Great Castle Head
description: In line, N.E. by E. ½ E., lead in mid-channel between St. Ann's Point & Mid-channel Rock

name: Pembroke Dockyard
description: In line, S.E. by E. ½ E., lead up. High light shown betw. W. by N. ¾ N. and N.W. ½ N. Low light betw. W. by N. ½ N. and N.N.E.; a green sector is shown over Carr Spit betw. N. ½ W. and N. by W. ½ W.

name: Neyland Pier
description: A fix. br. floating lt. off end of landing-pier... Bright leading lights shown for G. W. R. Co.'s vessels, two at Neyland Point and two at Hazelbeach, to clear shoal ground off Weare Point and Neyland Spit. Shown from huts, painted red and white.

name: SMALLS
character: One occulting bright or red light, 1 min.
description: Granite tower, 141 ft. high, red & white bands. Light eclipsed twice in quick succession, followed by 54 secs. light; bright seaward; red over Hats and Barrels Rocks between E. ½ S. and S.E. ¾ E.

name: SOUTH BISHOP ROCK
description: White tower, 36 ft. high

name: New Quay
character: One fix. bright or red lt.
description: On pier-head, September 15 to March 12. To southward of E. ½ N. the light is red

name: CARDIGAN BAY LT.-V.
character: One rev. red lt., ½ min.
description: In 35 fathoms, at 20 miles N. by W. from Port Cardigan

name: Aberystwith
character: 1. One fix. br. or red lt. 2. Two fix. br. Tide lts.
description: 1. On pier-head; light red to South and West, bright to W.N.W. and N.N.E. 2. Two lights in a field, over inner end of harbour, while sufficient water

name: ST. TUDWALL ROADS
character: 1. One occulting bright or red light 2. One lower fix. red lt.
description: 1. White tower, 35 feet high, on West island. Light vis. 8 secs., eclipsed 2 secs.; bright to westward betw. N. by E. and S. by W.; thence red to S.E.; thence br. to N.E. by E. ½ E., and thence red to N. by E. Obscured by East Island betw. N.E. ½ E. & E. by N. ½ N. 2. A red ray, with an arc of 15°, is shown over Carreg-y-trai, from E. by S. to E. ½ N., from window 16 ft. below main light

name: BARDSEY ISLAND
character: One occult. br. lt., ½ min.
description: A square white tower, 99 feet high. Light eclipsed for 3 secs. once in every ½ minute...

name: Llanddwyn Island
description: Visible between N.W. ½ N. and S.W. ¾ W.

name: Carnarvon
description: One fixed red light on pier-head

name: Gwydir
description: Fixed lt. on pier; red seaward, br. N. of N.E.

name: CARNARVON BAY LT.-V.
description: In 30 fathoms, at 12¾ miles S.W. by S. ½ S. from South Stack lt.-ho. Flashes bright, bright, and red. Red, with small ball over large one

name: SOUTH STACK ROCK
description: White tower, 84 ft. high. During fogs a smaller bright revolving light, 1 minute, at 90 ft., is shown at 65 yards W. by S. of lighthouse, between S. ½ W. and N.E. ¾ E. (In partial fogs the two revolving lights may appear as one irregular light)

name: Holyhead
character: 1. One flash. red lt., 7½ s. 2. One fixed bright lt. 3. One small red light 4. Fix. red and green lts.
description: 1. Lighthouse on breakwater. Fixed lt. visible between flashes, within 3 or 4 miles. 2. On end of wooden jetty; old harbour 3. On old pier-head; shown from N.E. ½ N. to N.E. by N. ½ N., to clear Platters, &c. 4. Red light on North side, green light on South side, of inner harbour

name: SKERRIES
character: One occulting bright lt., 1 min. Lower fixed red light
description: White tower, 75 ft. high. Upper lt. eclipsed 3 times in quick succession, followed by 50 secs. light; not visible over East Platters Rock, from S.S.E. to S.E. ½ S. Low red light shown over Ethel and Coal Rocks, from E. ½ S. to E. by N. ½ N.

name: Amlwch Port
description: On North pier; vis. betw. N.E. ½ N. & E. ½ N. Shown only when the harbour is practicable

name: LYNUS or ELIAN POINT
description: A white building, 36 ft. high. Light visible 8 secs.; eclipsed 2 secs. Masked to mark Middle Mouse and Dulas Rocks

name: Beaumaris
description: A fixed red light on pier

name: Penrhyn
description: Fix. green lt. on E. pier-hd.; red lt. on W. pier

name: MENAI, TRWYN-DU PT.
description: Tower, 96 ft. high, painted in black and white bands

name: GREAT ORMES HEAD
character: One fix. bright or red lt.
description: Square gray building, on cliff of North point. Lt. bright from N.W. by W. ¾ W. to E. ½ N., thence red to E. ½ S.

name: Llandudno
description: On pier-head. Lower red light, or red flag, when it is dangerous to come alongside

name: Rhyl
description: A fixed bright light on pier-head

name: River Dee Lightvessel
description: In 8 fathoms, at river entrance, 7½ miles within the bar

name: N.W. LIGHTSHIP
character: One rev. br. lt., ½ min.
description: In 13 fathoms, 8¾ miles N.W. ½ W. from Horse Channel Fairway Buoy. Black, with white streak; a black ball on fore-mast

name: BAR LIGHTVESSEL
description: In 7½ fathoms, 8¾ miles N. ¾ W. from Hoylake lighthouse, and 8 miles E. by S. ¾ S. from N.W. Lightship. Painted red. (It is intended to exhibit an experimental ELECTRIC light, showing a flash every half minute)

name: Hoylake
description: White towers, 64 and 42 ft. In line, S.W. by S. ¾ S., 1,200 feet apart, near the church. Light shown from low tower, and obscured West of N. ¾ W. High light discontinued...

name: Leasowe
description: White lighthouse, 110 feet high, on the shore, betw. the Mersey and Dee. Light is masked over the bay eastward of N.N.W.

name: BIDSTON
description: Stone tower, 68 ft. high, on the hill. Light is masked over bay eastward of N.W. by N. ¾ N.

name: Dove Beacons
description: One on each beacon. In line, S.E. ¾ S., 420 yds. apart, lead along channel till Rock and North Wall lights are in line E. ½ S.

name: ROCK
character: One rev. br. lt., ½ min.
description: White tower, 94 ft. high. Also a lower fix. br. lt. down Rock Channel, and up the Mersey, or black ball, while 11 ft. water in Rock Gut

name: North Docks Wall
character: One fix. br. or red lt.
description: Bright betw. S. by W. and N. by W. ¾ W., red over Formby Bank East of N. by W. ¾ W. In line with Rock light, bearing E. ½ S., indicates turning point betw. Horse and Rock Channels. In clear weather only, light is greatly diminished in intensity to South of W. by S.

name: Birkenhead New Pier
description: One fixed bright light

name: Formby Lightvessel
character: One rev. red lt., ½ m.
description: At the elbow of Crosby and Queen's Channels, 3½ miles E.S.E. from Bar lightvessel. Hull black, two masts, black ball at fore

name: Crosby Lightvessel
description: In 27 ft., on North side of channel, off the N.E. elbow of Burbo Bank. Red, with red ball at fore

name: Crosby Lighthouse
description: Square white tower, 74 ft., N. of the point. Lt. visible seaward betw. W. & N.W. by N. ¾ N.

name: Ribble River
description: S.E. of Stanner Point. Light visible 3½ min.; dark ½ minute

name: Lytham
description: Tide light on new pier, from 2h. before to 1½h. after high water

name: St. Anne's-on-Sea
description: Two fixed red lights on ends of pier

name: Southport
description: A fixed bright light on pier-head

name: Blackpool Piers
description: Green light on North pier, red lt. on South pier

name: Fleetwood
description: High lt. in town, low lt. on esplanade, N. ½ E. and S. ½ W., 850 ft. apart. Shown while 9 ft.

name: Wyre River
description: Red pile lighthouse on N.E. elbow of North Wharf Bank

name: Lune River
description: On Cockersand Point and Plover Scar Rock, while 8 ft. water. In line, E. by S. ½ S., 834 yds. apart; visible betw. S.W. and N. ½ W. A fixed bright tide light at Glasson Dock

name: Grange Channel Lt.-Ves.
description: In 17 feet, on N.W. side of Grange Channel, between Yeoman and Clark Wharf Spits. Approach to Morecambe. Also shows a bright light, or ball, while 8 ft. in channel to harbour

name: Morecambe Harbour
character: 1. One fixed bright lt. 2. Two fixed red lights 3. One fix. blue or red lt.
description: 1. White stone tower, 50 ft. high, at extremity of West or stone pier 2. One 130 yds. from end of stone pier, other 1 cable from end of wooden jetty, in line lead over bar 3. On promenade pier; blue seaward, red to harbour

name: MORECAMBE BAY LT.-V.
character: One rev. red lt., ½ min.
description: In 12 fathoms, 14¾ miles W. by S. from Walney lighthouse. Red ball at mast-head

name: WALNEY ISLAND
character: One rev. br. lt., 1 min. One fixed red light
description: Stone lt.-house, 60 ft. high, and mast, on S.E. point. In one, N.W. by W. ¾ W., 440 yards apart. Red lt. vis. to S. betw. W. and N.E.

name: Piel Bar Lightvessel
description: A small lightvessel, moored in 4 fathoms, about 3 cables seaward of Lightning Knoll Three sets of fixed bright leading lights, and several buoys bearing gas lights, mark direction of dredged channel

name: Piel Harbour
description: Bright lt. on Michael Scar. Red lt. on pier, br. to S.S.E. and N.W. in direction of channel

name: Barrow
character: 1. One fixed bright lt. 2. One fixed red light 3. One fixed red light 4. One fixed green lt.
description: 1. On East side of channel to Barrow, 1 mile N.W. ½ W. from Piel pier light 2. At Devonshire Dock entrance, 2 hours before to 2 hours after high water 3. At Ramsden Dock, when gates open 4. Pier on West side of Barrow Island

name: SELKER ROCKS LT.-V.
description: In 10½ fms., 3 miles W. ½ N. from Selker Point. A diamond at mast-head. Light shows one bright and one red flash every ½ minute

name: ST. BEES HEAD
character: One occulting bright lt., ½ min.
description: White tower, 55 ft. high. Light eclipsed twice in quick succession, followed by 24 secs. lt.; masked East of South (nearly), or one-third of a mile outside Selker Rocks

name: Whitehaven
character: 1. One rev. br. lt., 2 m. 2. One fixed green light 3. One fixed red light
description: 1. White tower, 47 ft. high, on West pier-head. 2. On North pier-head 3. On Old Quay; half-flood to half-ebb; red flag by day

name: Harrington
description: On pier-head, while 8 ft. water. Red drum at inner end of pier by day

name: Workington, Tide Lights
character: 1. One fixed bright lt. 2. Fix. green and red lts.
description: 1. On end of St. John's breakwater, while 8 ft. water; red ball at pier 2. Two green lights in one lead in. A red light on Old pier, South side of river

name: Maryport
character: 1. Two fixed lights 2. One fixed bright lt. 3. Two fixed lights
description: 1. Bright light on outer end of South pier, and red light on outer end of North pier 2. Tide light on inner end of South pier, wLile 8 ft. water in the harbour. If entrance obstructed, a red light is shown 12 ft. below 3. Green light on jetty on South side of harbour; red light on Tongue pier, on North side, while 8 ft. water

name: Solway Lightvessel
description: In 5 fathoms, in Robin Rigg Channel. Black, with ball

name: Lee Scar
description: On piles, on the rocks

name: Skinburness
description: A white building, 32 ft. high, on Cott or Silloth Point

name: Silloth
description: Yellow gas light on wooden pier, changed to green when 12 feet on dock sill. Two red lights in line lead through dock entrance

name: POINT OF AYRE
description: White stone tower, 99 ft. high, ½ mile S.W. of the point. Light bright and red alternately

name: Peel Harbour
description: Red light on end of old pier; bright light on end of North breakwater

name: Port Erin
description: New breakwater partly destroyed, and covered at high water; black buoy marks outer end. Lts., 130 ft. apart, on E. shore, in l[?]e lead in

name: CHICKEN ROCK
character: One rev. br. lt., ½ min.
description: Granite tower, 143 ft. high, [?] mile West from South extremity of Calf of Man

name: Port St. Mary
character: 1. Two fixed lights 2. One fixed green light
description: 1. Bright light on pier, in line with red light on hill on West side of port, lead in 2. On extremity of new breakwater at Port St. Mary Point

name: Castletown Harbour
description: On new pier-head. Visible seaward between the entrance points of the bay

name: LANGNESS
description: Lighthouse, 63 ft. high, on S.E. part of point. Light shows a flash every 5 secs.

name: Derby Haven
description: Fishing lt. on S.W. end of breakwater. (Aug. 12 to Oct. 10)

name: DOUGLAS
description: White stone tower, 65 feet high, on Douglas Head. Light obscured inshore of S.W. ¼ W.

name: Douglas Harbour
description: Red light on Battery pier. Bright light on inner pier, while 9 ft. on the bar

name: Douglas Bay
description: A blue light on end of promenade pier. Green light on end of Victoria pier, visible between E.N.E. and S. by E.

name: Ramsey Bay
description: Shown vertically, near extr. of landing-pier, at 600 yds. southward of harbour entrance...

name: Ramsey Harbour
description: Red light on South pier-head, green light on North pier-head

name: BAHAMA BANK LT.-V.
description: In 11 fathoms, off S.E. end of bank. Light shows 2 quick flashes, followed by 20 secs. darkness. Red, with ball

name: Clacton
description: One fixed red light on end of pier

name: HARWICH
description: Pile lt.-houses, 208 yds. apart, on shore abreast Dovercourt. In one, bearing N.W. by W. ½ W., lead betw. the Inner Ridge & Andrews buoys. High light shown from S. ½ E. to E. by N.; low light only shown between S.E. by E. and E. by S. ½ S.

name: Jetties
description: Red light on North jetty, visible betw. East and E. by N. ¾ N.; anchorage forbidden. Green light on West jetty and on East jetty Three fixed red lights on Parkeston quay, and a fixed red light on end of Felixtow pier

name: Landguard Point
character: One fix. red or br. lt.
description: A red light outside, betw. S.S.E. and S.W., to Beach End buoy; bright to West. A strip of red light betw. N.W. by N. ½ N. and N. by W. ½ W. to clear the North Shelf buoy. A fixed green light on Landguard Fort jetty...

name: Woodbridge Haven
description: Two small fixed bright lights on West side ...

name: Cork Lightvessel
character: One rev. br. lt., ½ min.
description: In 4½ fathoms, near Cork Ledge. Red, with ball at mast-head

name: SHIPWASH LT.-VESSEL
description: In 9 fathoms, off N.E. end of Sand. Red, with ball at mast-head. A long flash betw. two short flashes, followed by 14 secs. eclipse ...

name: Outer Gabbard Shoal
description: Lightvessel proposed

name: ORFORDNESS
character: Two fix. br. or red lts. (High light to South)
description: Towers, 99 and 72 ft. high, with red and white bands, S.W. ½ W. and N.E. ½ E., 1,439 yds. apart. In one, from South, lead through Hollesley Bay, but very close to the N.W. edge of the Whiting Sand; from North, between Sizewell Bank and Aldbro' Napes, &c. High light is red from W. by S. to W.S.W. over shoals in Hollesley Bay; the rest bright. Low light is red over Sizewell Bank, from N.E. to N.E. ¾ N.; then masked in-shore. The rest bright

name: Southwould
description: Three small fixed bright gas lights on the cliff

name: Kessingland or Pakefield
description: On cliff, N.E. side of Kessingland fish-houses; shown through Gat betw. E. ½ N. & S.E. ½ E.

name: LOWESTOFT
character: Upper rev. br. lt., ½ min. Lower occulting red or bright light, ½ min. (High light to North)
description: White lt.-houses, 53 and 48 ft. high, 830 yards apart, S.S.E. and N.N.W. High lt. on cliff, low lt. on ness. Low lt., eclipsed for 3 secs. every ½ min., is red over line of sands from N.N.E., seaward, to S.W. by S., and bright over in-shore channels. High lt.-ho. shows lower fixed red lt., betw. N.E. and N.E. by N., as a guide to round the ness. (The red lt. on N. pier is masked in-shore of N.E. by E. ½ E. for same purpose.) When red lt. from high tower opens from the northward, haul into red lt. from low lt.-ho. until N. pier red lt. opens, when run for it until low red lt. changes to bright

name: Lowestoft Harbour
description: Red lts. on pier-heads. Two green lts. at entr. of inner harb. Red lt. at fish-market when 10 ft. water, green when less. Green lt. at end of North pier works

name: Corton Lightvessel
description: Fairway light in 12½ fms., outside Corton Sand. Red, with half ball below usual ball

name: St. Nicholas Gat Lt.-Ves.
character: One fixed bright light One flash. red lt., 10 secs.
description: In 10 fathoms, at inner end of channel. Red, with ball. Red light on mizen-mast

name: Yarmouth, or Gorleston
character: 1. One fixed Tide light 2. Two fixed red lights
description: 1. On South pier. Light is red with flood tide (red flag by day), but green with ebb 2. In line, S.W. ½ S., clear Caistor Shoal; one on Sailor's Home, one on Britannia Pier A fixed green light on Britannia Pier-head

name: MIDDLE CROSS SAND LIGHTVESSEL
description: Painted red, with two broad vertical black stripes; two cones, points together, at the mast-head. In 19¾ fathoms, nearly 7 miles S. by W., westerly, from Newarp lightvessel. A 5-secs. flash followed by a short flash, then eclipsed 17½ secs. Explosive Rockets fired when a vessel is in dangerous proximity

name: Cockle Lightvessel
description: In 7 fathoms, at East side of North entrance of Cockle Gat. Red, with ball

name: WINTERTON NESS
description: A circular red tower, 69 ft. high. Lt. masked to S. by E. ½ E. to Scroby Elbow bell buoy

name: NEWARP LT.-VESSEL
description: In 17 fathoms, North end of sand, with three masts and balls. Light gives 3 quick flashes, then eclipsed 36 secs.

name: WOULD LIGHTVESSEL
description: In 15 fms., off South end of Hasborough Sand, 6 miles N. by W. ½ W. from Newarp lightvessel. Red, with diamond at mast-head

name: HASBOROUGH
character: One occult. br. lt., ½ m.
description: White tower, 85 feet high, S.S.E. of church. Lt. eclipsed for 5 secs. once in every ½ min.

name: HASBOROUGH LT.-VES.
description: In 14 fathoms, near North end of sand, 10 miles E. ½ S. from Cromer lighthouse; lights horizontal. Red, with two red balls

name: SMITH'S KNOLL LT.-V.
character: One 2-flash. red and br. light, 20 secs.
description: Red, with black bulwarks, and a black ball at mast-head. Moored in 25½ fms., 1 mile E. of the shoal, and 17½ miles S. ¾ E. from Leman and Ower lightvessel. Light shows a red and a bright flash, followed by 12 secs. eclipse

name: LEMAN & OWER LT.-V.
description: In 16 fathoms between the Sands. Light shows 2 quick flashes, followed by 20 secs. darkness. Red, two masts and balls

name: CROMER
description: White tower, 58 ft. high, near the cliff

name: HUNSTANTON
character: One occult. br. lt., ½ m.
description: White tower, 61 ft. high, on the point. Two quick occultations, followed by 24 secs. light. Red over Roaring Middle Sand, between W. by N. ¾ N. and N.W. by W. ¼ W.

name: Lynn Well Lightvessel
description: In 17½ fathoms, off the hook of the Long Sand. Red, with ball at mast-head

name: Lynn Channel Lt.-Vessel
description: Moored in 3½ fms., at N.E. end of Wisbeach Bar Flat, 8 miles above Lynn Well lt.-vessel

name: Lynn
description: Leading lights on East side of entrance to cut; in one, S. ¾ E., 555 ft. apart

name: Boston
description: Two fixed bright leading lights at Hob Hole

name: Skegness
description: Two fixed bright lights, vertical, at end of pier

name: Inner Dowsing Lt.-Ves.
description: In 10 fathoms, near N.E. end of shoal. Red, with two balls vertically

name: DUDGEON LT.-VESSEL
description: In 10½ fathoms, 1 mile S.W. of shoalest part. Red, with ball at mast-head. Two quick flashes, first bright, second red, followed by an eclipse of 22 secs.

name: OUTER DOWSING LT.-V.
character: One rev. red lt., ½ min.
description: In 10½ fathoms, on West side of shoal. Half ball over other ball

name: Spurn Lightvessel
description: In 9½ fathoms, off the point. Red, with ball at mast-head

name: SPURN POINT
character: 1. One occulting br. or red light, ½ min. 2. One fixed bright lt.
description: High lt.-house red, 112 ft. high; low lt.-house white, 76 ft. high. In line, N.W., 474 feet apart. High lt., eclipsed 3 secs. ev. ½ min., red between Sandhaile and Grimsby Pier, or from S.E. by S. to N.W. by W. ¾ W.

name: Bull Sand Lightvessel
description: In 5 fathoms, near S.E. side of Sand, off Spurn Point. Red, with ball

name: Grimsby
description: One on each pier-head of outer basin

name: Middle Sand Lt.-Vessel
description: In 3½ fathoms, on N.W. end. A fixed red light

name: Stallingborough Ferry
description: One fixed bright light to E.N.E.

name: Newsham Booth
description: About 1½ mile below Killingholme lights, South shore of river. An additional red sector from high lighthouse over Holme buoy No. 8

name: Killingholme
description: Two lights in line, N.W. ¾ W., lead up the river; and when S. ¾ W. lead down

name: Thorngumbald Clough
description: Two fixed bright leading lights

name: Salt End
description: Two fixed bright leading lights. Several small leading lights are shown on both shores of the river between Salt End and Faxfleet

name: Withernsea
description: A fixed red light at end of pier

name: Hornsea
description: Two fix. br. lts. vertical, at end of wrecked pier

name: Bridlington
description: On the North pier-head while 9 feet water in the harbour

name: FLAMBOROUGH HEAD
description: White tower, 87 ft. high. Light shows two bright faces and one red alternately.

name: Scarborough
description: On Vincent Pier while 9 ft. water in harb.; red seaward, bright toward harb. A ball by day

name: HIGH WHITBY
description: White towers, 66 and 46 ft. high, on Ling Hill; in one, S.S.E., 258 yds. apart. North light red over and inshore of Scar Rock. (One 3-flashing light proposed)

name: Whitby Harbour
character: 1. One fixed green light 2. One fix. red or gr. lt.
description: 1. Yellow lt.-ho., 60 ft. high, on W. pier. Lt. shown from 2h. before to 2h. after H.W. 2. E. Pier lt. red to S., but green to N. of Rock buoy. From 2h. before to 2h. after H.W.

name: Coatham
description: Red light on outer end of pier (Light proposed on outer end of Redcar Rocks)

name: South Gare Breakwater
description: White tower on extremity. Light obscured southward of E.S.E. over Redcar Rocks

character: 1. Fourth buoy, fixed green light 2. Fifth buoy, fix. red lt. 3. Seal Sand, fix. red lt.
description: 1. On East training wall, 3½ cables N.E. by E. from Fifth buoy light 2 and 3. 1,200 yds. apart; in one, S.W. ¾ W., mark for Fairway buoy, and lead in. There are six small lights up the Tees

name: Seaton
description: High light bright, ½ mile inland; low light red

name: HARTLEPOOL
character: One fixed bright light, and low red Tide light
description: Yellow lt.-ho., 73 ft. high, on the Heugh. The red tide lt., or red ball, from ½-flood to ½-ebb

name: Old Harbour
description: Fix. red lt. on pier; 2 red leading lts. on quay

name: West Harbour
description: One fixed green light on N. pier. Two red lts. in one, N.W. ½ N., lead in, while 10 ft. water

name: Seaham
character: Upper fixed bright lt., low rev. red lt., ½ min.
description: In one stone tower, 58 feet high, on Red Acre Point A fixed red tide light on South pier-head when practicable

name: Sunderland
character: 1. Two fixed lights 2. One fixed br. Tide lt.
description: 1. Upper bright, lower red, in a white tower, 64 ft. high, on North pier-head 2. On South pier, from ½-flood till 2h. after H.W., and during the last 2h. a bright light is shown beneath it; a green light below it shows danger

name: SOUTER POINT
character: One rev. br. lt., ½ min. lower fix. br. or red lt.
description: White tower, 76 ft. high. ELECTRIC light. Low light from S. by E. to S. ¾ W.; thence red to S. by W. ¾ W. over Whitburn Stile, Hendon Rocks, &c.

name: TYNEMOUTH
description: White tower, 79 ft. high, near Priory ruins, in the castle. Light visible seaward between N. by E. ½ E. and S.W. ½ S.

name: Tyne North Pier
description: Vertical, on North Pier Works. A red light at middle of North pier

name: Tyne South Pier
character: One occulting bright or red light, 10 secs.
description: Groyne on Herd Sand. Lt. bright over N. pier and entr. betw. N.E. by E. ¾ E. and E. ½ S.; thence red to S.E. by E. ¾ E., over S. pier

name: Tyne River
description: At North Shields. White towers, 49 and 76 ft. high; in one, W. ¾ N., 240 yards apart

name: Blyth
character: 1. Two fix. br. Tide lts. 2. Two fixed lights
description: 1. At South end of town, while 8 ft. water on bar; in one, N. by W. ¾ W. A blue flag by day 2. Upper red, lower bright, on S.W. end of extension of East pier

name: Newbiggin
description: Fixed lt., red seaward, during herring season

name: COQUET ISLAND
character: Two fixed bright or red lights in one tower
description: White tower, 72 ft. high, on S.W. part. Upper light bright seaward between S. ½ W. and N. by E. ½ E.; thence red to N. by E., over Bulmer Bush Rocks, &c. Lower light bright from S.E. by S. ¾ S. to S. by E.; thence westward is red over Bondicar Bush, to S. by W. ½ W.

name: Warkworth
character: One fix. br. cr red Tide lt.
description: On S. pier, while 10 ft. water on the bar. Shows bright S. of E. by S. ½ S., and red northward

name: North Sunderland
character: Two fix. lts., red and br.
description: Leading lights on pier, from ½-flood to ¾-ebb. In line, bear S.W. by W. ½ W.

name: FARN ISLAND
character: Upper flashing light ev. 20 secs. Lower fixed bright light
description: Two white towers, 43 and 27 ft. high; in one, N. by W. ½ W., 187 yds. apart. High light, near S.W. point, shows two bright flashes and one red flash: a flash every 20 secs. Low light, near N.W. point, visible between N.W. by N. ½ N. and N. by W.

name: LONGSTONE
character: One rev. br. lt., ½ min.
description: Red tower, 85 ft. high, on West side of rock. Dangers extend over ¾ of a mile to N.E.

name: Berwick-on-Tweed
character: Two fix. lts., br. and red
description: In one tower, 44 ft. high, on pier-head. Upper light bright. Lts. not visible W. of Seal Carr Ledges. Low red lt. only while 10 ft. on bar

name: Burnmouth
description: Bright fishing light on pier, when safe, and red and bright leading lights

name: Eyemouth
description: Leading lights, upper red and lower bright

name: ST. ABB'S HEAD
description: White tower, 29 ft. high. A flash ev. 10 secs.

name: Coldingham
description: Red and green lights occasionally on piers

name: Dunbar
description: Old Harbour lt. bright toward entrance; green to W.; red to E. Red lt. at Victoria Harbour. Additional lights in fishing season

name: North Berwick
description: Fish. lt. on N. pier, red seawd. On dark nights

name: FIDRA ISLAND
description: Lighthouse, 56 feet high, near summit of island. Lt. shows two quick flashes

name: Port Seton
description: Fish. lt. on E. pier, red seawd. On dark nights

name: Cockenzie
